Faceless Studio · image models

Which FLUX makes the specimen

Every image below was generated today on Cloudflare Workers AI, from one identical prompt, for the job the pipeline actually needs: a specimen shot that no stock library holds.

The prompt, unchanged across all three

Extreme macro cross-section of ancient Roman concrete: coarse grey volcanic mortar embedded with angular basalt aggregate and crushed terracotta fragments, one bright chalky white lime clast at the centre with a fine dark crack running through it, scientific specimen photography, diffuse even lighting, sharp focus, no text, no people

Not a lucky frame

The left image is the same subject run a second time through FLUX.2 dev, via the pipeline's real code path rather than a probe. The right is an unrelated subject, to show the gain is not specific to grey rock.

So: FLUX, or NotebookLM through a browser?

What FLUX.2 gives you now

  • Free. Every FLUX model is billed in neurons against the 10,000/day allowance. My earlier note that FLUX.2 cost dollars was simply wrong.
  • Cheaper than what it replaces. ~150 neurons against 326, so roughly 66 images a day instead of 30.
  • Already wired. fvs image --model dev|klein|schnell, dev by default.
  • No account exposure and nothing to maintain.

What NotebookLM would cost to find out

  • It does generate images — but nlm cannot download them, so extraction needs a headless browser.
  • Watermark unknown. NotebookLM infographics carry a burned-in “Gemini Notebook” mark. Nobody has checked standalone images.
  • Session dies in about an hour, against an undocumented UI that changes on Google’s schedule.
  • Same risk class we already accepted for nlm — I am not going to pretend it is a new one.
Today’s 10,000-neuron allowance is spent, so the four further subjects I queued could not render — the vision check and reranker used during the last two video rebuilds consumed most of it. It resets daily. If you want the NotebookLM question settled with evidence rather than argument, generate one image there by hand and save it; comparing it against these takes two minutes.
